blocks.raw:
<Tip>
**Memory Aid:** Shallow footings are direct pushers—they shove load straight down into soil. Deep piles and caissons are deep anchors—they hang onto the soil with friction or grip a firm layer with their tip. Mats are load-spreaders—they flatten pressure across a wide area to reduce settlement. Floating foundations are weight-balancers—they remove as much soil weight as they place in structure.
</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Assuming shallow foundations are always cheaper; deep foundations are often mandatory in soft soil and eliminate costly settlement repair later.","Confusing floating foundation with a raft foundation; floating requires Df and excavation weight to nearly equal structure weight; ordinary mats are intermediate supports, not floating.","Treating combined footing and mat as equivleant; combined footings support 2–4 columns; mats cover the entire footprint and provide greater stiffness and load distribution.","Placing mats at arbitrary depth; mat depth is selected to balance bearing capacity and settlement. Deeper mats reduce pressure but increase cost. Optimization is required.","Omitting the role of groundwater and compressibility in foundation selection; soft, saturated clays mandate deep foundations and settlement monitoring, not shortcuts to shallow systems."]} />
